files.README.md:
# Provingkit

Agent plugins for Claude Code and Codex: Mergecraft, Versionkeeping, Rolecasting, Tricritical, and more. Each member lives under `plugins/`.
files.AGENTS.md:
# Repository instructions

Agents working on this repository's pull requests run the Kit as built from this checkout. `scripts/install_local.sh` installs it under `.cache/claude-plugins/provingkit/`; rerun it after changing anything under `plugins/`.

Use Conventional Commits. Prefix branches with `ivan/`.
files.CONTRIBUTING.md:
# Contributing

Open a pull request against `main`. CI (`validate`, `test`) must pass, every review conversation must be resolved, and one approving review is required before merge. Squash-merge is the default.

How agents handle review threads is defined by Mergecraft's `getting-prs-merged` skill in `plugins/mergecraft/`.
files.scripts/install_local.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Install the plugins from this checkout for local agents.
set -eu
root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
for plugin in "$root"/plugins/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$plugin")
  version=$(sed -n 's/.*"version": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json")
  dest="$root/.cache/claude-plugins/provingkit/$name/$version"
  rm -rf "$dest" && mkdir -p "$dest" && cp -R "$plugin". "$dest"
done

# Getting PRs merged

Drive one pull request to a verified merge. Before resolving any review thread, read [review-thread resolution](references/review-thread-resolution.md).

# Review-thread resolution

Decide when a pull request's unresolved review threads may be resolved, and by whom. Resolution runs only through `scripts/resolve_review_thread.py`. Being able to resolve a thread is never permission to.

## Ownership rules

Follow any written rule that assigns resolution ownership in this repository, its organization, or its agent instructions. A rule scoped to another repository does not apply.

## Human-authored threads

A human reviewer's thread belongs to that reviewer, whatever the pull request's urgency.

- After the thread is addressed, reply on it with the commit that addressed it, `@`-mention the reviewer, and ask them to resolve the conversation if the change covers it. Request re-review if they submitted a review.
- Do not resolve the thread on the reviewer's behalf, however long they take. While it is open, report it as the remaining gate and who has to act.
- A maintainer's explicit direction on the pull request to resolve a named thread is the only exception.

## Bot-authored threads

Leave a known auto-resolver's threads (CodeRabbit) to its own review. Resolve other bots' addressed threads after brief research.

# Getting PRs merged

Drive one pull request to a verified merge. Before resolving any review thread, read [review-thread resolution](references/review-thread-resolution.md).

# Review-thread resolution

Decide when a pull request's unresolved review threads may be resolved, and by whom. Resolution runs only through `scripts/resolve_review_thread.py`. Being able to resolve a thread is never permission to.

## Ownership rules

Follow any written rule that assigns resolution ownership in this repository, its organization, or its agent instructions. A rule scoped to another repository does not apply.

## Human-authored threads

Without a written rule, the thread's commenter or a maintainer owns resolution at first.

- After the thread is addressed, reply on it and `@`-mention the reviewer. Request re-review if they submitted a review. Their clock starts at that notice.
- Wait 48 hours for a nonurgent pull request, 4 hours for a stated deadline, and not at all when the operator says it is urgent.
- When the longest remaining wait across the unresolved human threads reaches zero and they are the last gate, the agent becomes the owner: resolve each of them once and continue to the merge.

## Bot-authored threads

Leave a known auto-resolver's threads (CodeRabbit) to its own review. Resolve other bots' addressed threads after brief research.

# Versionkeeping

Git safety for agents: baselines, task-only commits, exact-lease publication, and provenance-aware cleanup.

## Skills

- `checkpointing-and-publishing-git-work`
- `using-persistent-git-worktrees`
- `resolving-merge-conflicts`
- `syncing-forks-with-upstream`

## Worktrees

Branch work happens in a persistent worktree beside the primary checkout:

```sh
git worktree add ../<checkout>.wt/<branch> -b <branch>
```

Keep the primary checkout on `main`.
